summary: Surgery (Holy Bible + Ankh): each time you would die, 40% chance it pays your whole Debt and sends you to the next Deadline. Breaks after 3 saves.
tip: A 40% death save that ignores how big the debt is, so it shines late. Horseshoe raises it to 80%. Holy Bible and Ankh stay out of the store while it is equipped.

effects.note: Rolled only when you are about to die (after the death countdown), not every spin; the charm breaks after its third successful save.

synergies.why: Doubles the save chance from 40% to 80%.
Discard it after fusing Ra's Book to get Holy Bible and Ankh back, keeping all three safety nets.
However far Limbo inflates the debt, a successful save pays all of it.

assumptions: Each would-be death rolls the 40% once; the charm breaks after its third successful save.
Assumed a save pays the remaining debt for you, so the coins in hand are kept (the wiki Coin page suggests it pays by handing you coins).
The break after 3 saves is written as discardAfter on the death-save effect; the engine does not shorten the life of death-save or event-triggered effects, so it is not misread as a one-Round charm.
Both Ankh and Ra's Book act at the Dying step (wiki Charm Activation page), so like Ankh it can probably wait in a drawer and be equipped during the death countdown.
Wiki: while a Surgery charm is equipped, its ingredients (Holy Bible, Ankh) are banned from the store.

summary: Surgery (Cat Food + Toy Train): after 3 spins in a row with no reward, you get 2 extra spins with Luck +8.
tip: Early builds miss about half their spins, so it fires roughly every other Round. It fades as Luck and symbol boosts make misses rare; Depression keeps the misses coming.

effects.note: In the game both extra spins get Luck +8; the engine cannot put Luck on extra spins, so the Luck goes on the spin right after the streak instead. That counts one lucky spin instead of two, so the engine shows roughly half the real gain.

synergies.why: Both fire after 3 straight misses: Symbols grow for good, then the lucky spins cash in.
Both fire after 3 straight misses: Patterns grow for good, then the lucky spins cash in.
Without the machine's own Luck, miss streaks come more often, so it fires more.
The empty spins that set off Cat Toy are the ones that can grow all Symbols.
Discard it after fusing Cat Toy to get Cat Food back: +2 spins every Round on top.

antiSynergies.why: Three misses in a Round trigger Luck +8 spins that almost always score, ruining the empty Round Bullet Train needs.

assumptions: Assumed it can fire again if the miss streak continues (every 3 misses in a row).

Simulator: plain builds miss about 50-55% of spins, giving roughly 0.4-0.6 triggers per 7-spin Round; builds with symbol-chance boosts or Luck charms (20-35% misses) trigger it only 0.05-0.2 times per Round.

Simulated with Luck +8 on both extra spins it is worth about +95-115% coins in plain Deadline 2-4 builds, +25-55% in mid builds and under +10% in focused Luck builds; the engine encoding shows about half of that.

summary: Surgery (Hamsa + Rotated Hamsa): every Pattern triggers twice during the whole first Round of each Deadline, and the whole last Round has Luck +4.
tip: One slot covering a whole retriggered Round and a whole Luck+4 Round each Deadline, versus 3 spins each (Luck+7 on the lucky ones) from the two Hamsas. Cat Food adds 2 spins to both Rounds.

synergies.why: +2 spins in the first and last Rounds: 2 more retriggered and 2 more lucky spins per Deadline.
Doubled Patterns all first Round push many spins to 5+, growing its multiplier.
Press it in the retriggered first Round: every scored symbol is scored twice, so it grows twice.
Retriggered spins reach 5+ Patterns more easily, doubling Symbols for the rest of the Round.
Discard it after the fusion to get Hamsa and Rotated Hamsa back; their first- and last-spin bonuses stack on top.
With one Round per Deadline, that Round should be both first and last: every spin gets the retrigger and Luck +4.

assumptions: With only one Round in a Deadline, that Round should count as both first and last and get both bonuses (not verified).
Extra Rounds (Music Tape, Weird Clock, Rage) presumably shift which Round is last rather than adding bonus Rounds.

summary: Surgery (Consolation Prize + Midas Touch), triggers randomly (40%): every Symbol scored that spin gains its base value for good, like Golden on all of them.
tip: Passive Midas Touch on 40% of spins: one of the best scaling charms. Horseshoe makes it 80%; retriggers and Luck mean more scored symbols to grow. Take it as early as you can.

effects.note: Not a real Golden modifier: on 40% of spins every scored Symbol grows by its base value, which on average equals a 40% Golden chance on every Symbol; written this way so the engine counts growth per scored symbol (retriggers included).

synergies.why: Doubles the trigger chance to 80%.
Force a trigger before a big Luck or Jackpot spin to grow everything it scores.
A whole Round of retriggers scores every symbol twice, doubling the growth on triggering spins.
Discard it after the fusion to get Midas Touch and Consolation Prize back: two more ways to grow every Symbol.
Luck +7 lays down many matching symbols on the last spin, so a trigger there grows a lot at once.

assumptions: Read like Midas Touch (same wording): each scored symbol, retriggers included, adds its base value to that Symbol, so growth scales with how many symbols you score.

The engine has no per-scored-symbol growth outside the Golden modifier, so the effect is written as a 40% Golden chance; Horseshoe's doubling is not seen by the engine, and in the simulator it shares a cell's single modifier slot with real modifier chances.

summary: Surgery (Lover 1 + Lover 2): forces a 666 on the last spin of Rounds 1 and 2 every Deadline; in the last Round every Symbol gets +30% Revenge chance.
tip: Only for 666 builds: two sure 666s a Deadline feed Baphomet, Book of Shadows and Rage, and Revenge repays part of the losses. Otherwise it wipes two Rounds of coins every Deadline from Deadline 3.

effects.text: A 666 is forced on the last spin of Rounds 1 and 2 of every Deadline. Each one wipes the coins earned that Round (Deadlines 3-6) or all coins in hand (Deadline 7+), triggers every 666 charm and drops a missing Cadaver piece into a drawer.

effects.note: Revenge: each scored Revenge symbol pays 5% of all coins lost to 666 so far this run.

synergies.why: Two sure 666s every Deadline double Above and Below twice per Deadline, for good.
Each forced 666 adds spins after the wipe, so the Round can earn again (and roll more 666s for your devil charms).
Doubles every Revenge payout to 10% of your 666 losses.
Two of the three 666s it needs come free each Deadline: one more and you get an extra Round.
Each forced 666 has a 35% chance to be cancelled, saving that Round's coins while 666 charms still fire.
Its sure 666s drop Corpse pieces into your drawers: the rare part of Sacrifice, Sin, Resurrection and Eternal Rest.

antiSynergies.why: From Deadline 7 a 666 takes all coins in hand, the pile Sin wants you to hold, twice per Deadline.
Every 666 resets the Sigil's Rising growth, and Lust makes two each Deadline.

assumptions: Assumed the forced 666 costs coins like a natural one (from Deadline 3, per the coin rules); unclear whether it also happens in Deadlines 1-2.
Unknown whether the new last spin after Book of Shadows' extra spins is forced to 666 again.
The engine cannot force 666s or value Revenge, so its effects are not simulated; ratings carry it, and the build's coin estimate will be too high while it is equipped.
Wiki: a 666 drops a Cadaver piece only while pieces are missing, replacing a stored charm if all drawers are full; a piece left in a drawer at Deadline end is discarded.
Wiki (Golden Horseshoe strategy): a 666 cancelled by Rosary still counts as seen for 666 charms, with no coin loss.

summary: Surgery (Greedy King + Naughty Dealer + Raging Capitalist): every Symbol has a 10% chance of a random modifier, +10% per other Surgery charm on your table.
tip: The payoff for stacking fusions: with 3 other Surgery charms it reaches 40%, spread over Golden, Chain, Repetition, Rising, Ticket and the rest. Alone it is weaker than its three ingredients.

effects.text: The 10% grows by another 10% for each other Surgery charm on the table (e.g. 40% with three others), split the same way across all modifiers.

synergies.why: Its Copy modifiers turn into the nearest other modifier, adding more of the mix, and it counts as another Surgery charm (+10%).
Its extra space holds more Surgery charms, and it counts as one itself (+10%).
Adds its own Rising chance on top and counts as another Surgery charm (+10%).
Drops a random Surgery charm into a drawer; equip it for another +10%.
Counts as a Surgery charm while equipped; discard it to get the three ingredients back.

assumptions: Assumed the modifier is picked evenly among all 10 kinds (Golden, Token, Ticket, Repetition, Battery, Chain, Investor, Rising, Copy, Revenge).
Only the base 10% is simulated; the engine cannot count Surgery charms on the table, so the bonus from them is carried by the ratings.
Charms that take no space are used up at once and do not stay on the table, so they do not count.

summary: Surgery (Steam + Diesel Locomotive): every Round you finish without earning any coins permanently doubles both the Symbols and Patterns Multipliers.
tip: Fish for empty Rounds: pick 3 spins in a Round you can spare (about 15% end empty, 25% with Depression) and park Luck charms in a drawer. Each success is x4 coins for good.

effects.text: Each Round that ends with zero coins earned permanently doubles the Symbols Multiplier and doubles the Patterns Multiplier (x4 coins per trigger, compounding).

synergies.why: With no spontaneous Luck, a 3-spin Round ends empty about 25% of the time instead of 15%.
A sacrificed Round ends at once with no coins earned, which should count as an empty Round.
Fishing Rounds are full of empty spins, each a 25% chance to grow all Symbols.
Discard it after the fusion to get both Locomotives back; they grow on the same miss streaks.

antiSynergies.why: Three misses trigger Luck +8 spins that almost always score, so the Round is no longer empty.
Luck +7 on every Round's last spin nearly always scores something.
Two misses in a row trigger Luck +5, which usually breaks the empty Round.

assumptions: Simulator: 7-spin Rounds almost never end empty; 3-spin Rounds do about 15-18% of the time in plain builds (about 24% with Depression).
Unclear whether Interest or other coins paid at Round end count as earning coins.
Unverified: if a 666 that wipes the Round's coins counts as earning nothing, Lust's forced 666s would trigger it; not listed as a synergy.
The engine has no 'empty Round' trigger, so the doubling is kept as text and the ratings carry its value.

summary: Surgery (Necronomicon + Pentacle): every Symbol has a 10% Rising chance, +1% per spin with 5+ Patterns (up to 50%); a 666 resets the growth.
tip: Each scored Rising symbol adds +1 Symbols Multiplier until the Deadline ends, so it explodes in retrigger and Luck builds. Unlike Necronomicon it adds no 666 risk; Holy Bible guards the growth.

effects.note: The extra chance falls back to the base 10% whenever you score a 666.

synergies.why: Cancels 666s, so the Rising chance you built up is not reset.
A whole Round of retriggers pushes many spins past 5 Patterns and scores Rising symbols twice.
Retriggers push spins to 5+ Patterns, growing the chance faster.
Discard it after the fusion to get Pentacle and Necronomicon back; Necronomicon's 666 chance will reset the growth, though.
Adds a little more Rising chance, and the Sigil counts as a Surgery charm for Mad Emperor's +10% bonus.

antiSynergies.why: Forces two 666s every Deadline, resetting the growth each time.
+1.5% 666 chance means more resets of the Rising growth.

assumptions: cap is the extra growth on top of the 10% base (50% total).
Assumed a 666 resets the chance to the base 10%, and a 666 cancelled by Holy Bible or Rosary does not count as scored.
The engine counts the growth as a flat +2% Rising chance; in builds with frequent 5+ Pattern spins the real growth is far larger, which the ratings carry.
Rising lasts until the Deadline ends, so most of its value shows within the Deadline (power), not as permanent growth.

summary: Surgery (all four Aces): if you score all 7 Symbols at least once in the same Round, every Symbol's value doubles for good.
tip: Very hard to trigger: a normal Round almost never scores all 7 Symbols. A Round with an extra 2-symbol Pattern from Angel's Hand does about 10-20% of the time; otherwise the four Aces are worth more.

effects.note: scoredAll with all 7 Symbols is read per Round by the engine (share of Rounds that score every Symbol at least once).

synergies.why: Each press adds a 2-symbol Pattern for the Round, so rare Symbols score with just a pair: that Round hits all 7 about 10-20% of the time.
+2 spins per Round, more chances to score every Symbol.
Discard it after the fusion to get the four Aces back and keep their steady growth (needs all four drawers free).

antiSynergies.why: Your most valuable Symbol never appears, so all 7 can never be scored.
One Symbol fills about 45% of the grid, so the others form far fewer Patterns.

assumptions: Simulator: Rounds that score all 7 Symbols are about 0% in plain builds and 0.5% with Cat Food, Hamsas and Platinum Record; a Round with one extra 2-symbol Pattern does it 7-17% of the time (15-30% with Cat Food and Rotated Hamsa).
The engine reads scoredAll over all 7 Symbols as a per-Round rate, so the doubling is valued as permanent growth at that rate.

summary: Surgery (Electricity Meter, Potato Battery, Super Capacitor, Dynamo): button charms refill before each spin, but each press doubles your Debt for good.
tip: A trap for most builds: each press doubles the debt for the rest of the run. Only worth a few early presses of permanent-growth charms like Midas Touch; Nuclear Button gets more out of each press.

effects.note: Every Red Button charm is full before each spin. Left unsimulated on purpose: the engine would press every button charm on every spin without paying the debt doubling.
Each press of the Red Button doubles the Debt for the rest of the run.

synergies.why: Refilled before every spin, it can be pressed every Round instead of every 4th; each press still doubles the Debt, so only a few early ones pay off.
Every press triggers button charms twice while the debt still doubles only once per press.
A lucky save pays the debt in full, however many times it was doubled.

antiSynergies.why: Button charms already refill before every spin, so the call is wasted.
Refilled every spin, it invites more presses, and each one adds Limbo's own 100-500% Debt on top of the doubling.

assumptions: Assumed the doubling counts each press of the Red Button, not each charm it triggers.
Neither effect is simulated: refills every spin would make the engine press every charm each spin, and a debt rise per press cannot be modelled. The ratings carry its value.
The wiki Red Button page says it restores 1 charge to every button charm at the end of each spin; the item text (full recharge before each spin) is used here.

summary: Surgery (Dear Diary + Fidelity Card), triggers randomly (40%): when you buy a Charm, the store slot you bought it from refills with a new one.
tip: More offers per visit without paying for restocks, so it only helps when you have tickets to spend. It gives no discount, and Fidelity Card stays out of the store while it is equipped.

effects.text: 40% chance on each Charm purchase: the emptied store slot is restocked with a new Charm. Does not apply to Charms that restock the whole store when bought (Cigarettes).

synergies.why: Doubles the refill chance to 80%.
More Charms to buy means more purchases, each raising its Ticket chance by 1%.
A profitable buy (+2 net tickets) that can refill its own slot.
Discard it after the fusion to get Fidelity Card back, so refilled slots are also cheaper.

assumptions: Assumed the refill is free and is not a real store restock, so restock-triggered charms (Bell Pepper, Electricity Meter) do not fire on it.
Wiki: its ingredients (Dear Diary, Fidelity Card) are banned from the store while it is equipped.

summary: Surgery (Horseshoe + Nuclear Button + Sacred Heart): Red Button charms trigger one extra time per press, with a 30% chance of yet another.
tip: Nuclear Button without the lost charm slot, plus a bonus roll. Best with strong button charms such as Midas Touch, Number 1 or Cross. Needs Sacred Mode, since Sacred Heart is a Sacred charm.

effects.text: Triggers randomly (30%): charms triggered by the Red Button trigger one more time on top of the guaranteed extra trigger.
effects.note: Kept as text: the engine treats any extra trigger as guaranteed, which would overvalue a 30% roll.

synergies.why: Each press makes every symbol scored that Round grow two or three times.
Each press flips it down and back up: +1 Patterns Multiplier per press; the 30% bonus flip can leave it face down (+3% 666) until your next press.
Yellow Patterns retrigger two or three extra times for the whole Round.
Per a wiki note it can guarantee the 30% roll, and the pair can glitch into up to 99,999 triggers.
Discard it after the fusion to get Nuclear Button, Sacred Heart and Horseshoe back on top.

assumptions: Assumed the 30% roll is per press, giving 2.3 triggers per press on average (2.6 if Horseshoe doubles the roll).
Horseshoe is one of its ingredients, so it is banned from the store while the Trumpet is equipped; only Black Hole brings it back.
Sacred Heart only comes from Sacred Mode's 'Help!!' call, so this fusion needs a Sacred run.
Wiki: its ingredients are banned from the store while it is equipped.

summary: Surgery (Scratch and Hope + Expired Meds): one random Symbol appears far more often (+4); the Symbol re-rolls at the end of every Deadline.
tip: A huge Pattern boost whatever the Symbol: it fills about 40-50% of the grid. Lean on Pattern-count and big-Pattern charms, since the boosted Symbol changes every Deadline.

effects.note: The boosted Symbol is random (rolled when obtained, per the wiki) and changes every Deadline; Treasure, the one shown in the description, stands in for it.

effects.text: At the end of every Deadline the boosted Symbol changes to a random one.

synergies.why: Spins with 5+ Patterns become common, growing its multiplier fast.
7+ Pattern spins become realistic, each paying double your Interest.
Big Patterns show up most spins, stacking Pattern value for the Round.
Luck +7 usually picks the boosted Symbol, which then floods the grid toward a Jackpot.
Discard it after the fusion to get Scratch and Hope back: +1 more on the boosted Symbol, since it is the most likely one.

antiSynergies.why: One Symbol crowds out the others, so scoring all 7 in a Round gets even rarer.

assumptions: The engine cannot follow a random Symbol, so Treasure is used as a stand-in; when yours is a cheap Symbol the real gain is lower, on a Seven higher.
Wiki: the listed Symbol is randomized when the charm is acquired.

summary: Surgery (Shopping Cart + Fake Coin), takes no slot: doubles the free restocks you hold (10% chance to lose them all instead); with none, gives 2.
tip: Save up free restocks first (Crowbar, CloverBell, Gambler Traits), then fuse. A new Shopping Cart bought afterwards turns the doubled pile into Symbols Multiplier.

effects.note: Only when you hold no free restocks.

effects.text: Instant: doubles the free restocks you hold, but with a 10% chance they are reset to 0 instead.

synergies.why: A new Cart bought after the fusion gives +2 Symbols Multiplier for each of the doubled restocks.
Its +3 free restocks become +6 after the fusion.
You start each Deadline with 2 free restocks, so there is always a pile to double.
+3 free restocks per Clover and Bell spin build a big pile to double.

assumptions: Read as: double the pile, 10% chance to reset it to 0, and +2 only when you hold none; it may also give 2 right after a reset.
Assumed Shopping Cart can show up in the store again, since a no-space charm is used up and is not equipped.

summary: Surgery (Property Certificate + Sardines): +3 charm space while equipped. It uses one slot itself, so you net two extra charm slots.
tip: An easy upgrade if you own Property Certificate, since Sardines is otherwise dead weight: the fusion turns +1 net slot into +2. Black Hole can return the Certificate for +5 space in all.

synergies.why: Discard it after the fusion to get Property Certificate back: +5 charm space from two slots.
Room for more Surgery charms, and Beach Hotel counts as one itself (+10%).
Its extra space easily absorbs Hourglass's -1.

assumptions: Wiki: Property Certificate is banned from the store while Beach Hotel is equipped, so stacking both needs Black Hole.

summary: Surgery (The Collector + Dark Lotus): Avid Traits give Symbols Multiplier x2 instead of +2, and Ambitious Traits give Patterns Multiplier x2 instead of +1.
tip: Each Avid or Ambitious charm becomes a doubling, and several stack (x4, x8...). Avid beats its +2 once the rest of your Symbols Multiplier is above 2. Feed it with the Yellow/Orange betting calls.

effects.text: Each equipped charm with the Avid Trait gives Symbols Multiplier x2 instead of +2, and each one with the Ambitious Trait gives Patterns Multiplier x2 instead of +1; several of them multiply together.

synergies.why: Each Avid Trait it adds becomes a x2 Symbols Multiplier.
Each Ambitious Trait it adds becomes a x2 Patterns Multiplier.
Every store charm comes with a Trait, so Avid and Ambitious charms show up often.
Puts Traits on every store charm: grab the Avid and Ambitious ones.
Discard it after the fusion to get The Collector back, which adds +1 Patterns Multiplier per traited charm.

assumptions: Read as each Trait doubling its own multiplier (Avid: Symbols, Ambitious: Patterns). The text could also mean each such Trait gives both x2; that reading would make it much stronger.
The engine applies Traits as +2 / +1 and cannot rewrite them, so the doubling is kept as text and the ratings carry it.

summary: Surgery (Jimbo + D20), takes no slot: drops a random Surgery charm into a free drawer, no recipe needed.
tip: A lottery ticket for a Legendary fusion: it can roll Beach Hotel or First Place Prize, or a dud like Poker Deck. Jimbo alone is often worth about as much as the gamble.

synergies.why: The Surgery charm it drops adds another +10% once you equip it.
Surgeries cost no coins, so the gamble only costs its two ingredients.
Fuse it after Black Hole is made: discarding Black Hole then returns Jimbo and D20, so you keep the random Surgery charm too.

assumptions: Assumed any Surgery charm can be rolled, with equal odds; whether Apocalypse can appear is unknown.
The engine cannot value a random charm, so the ratings describe an average roll.

summary: Surgery (Corpse Left Arm + Cross), Red Button: ends the Round at once; Patterns Multiplier +1 for good per spin given up, -1 per spin already played.
tip: Press it before your first spin: +7 Patterns Multiplier for good (+9 with Cat Food). Sacrifice Rounds you can spare; other charged button charms fire on the same press, so park them first.

effects.text: Red Button (1 charge): lose all spins left this Round and end it now. Patterns Multiplier +1 for each spin given up and -1 for each spin already played this Round, permanently (+7 if pressed before the first spin of a 7-spin Round).

effects.note: Usage model: one full 7-spin Round sacrificed per Deadline. Written as a Red Button effect, the engine would assume a sacrifice every Round with no lost income.
Usage model: the sacrificed Round earns no coins.

synergies.why: +2 spins per Round: each sacrifice gives +9 Patterns Multiplier instead of +7.
A sacrificed Round ends with no coins earned, which should also double both multipliers.
The sacrificed Round still ends normally, so Sin doubles your held coins without playing a spin.
With Resurrection, Sin and Eternal Rest it fuses into Apocalypse, which restarts the run keeping your table.
Its extra Round can be sacrificed for +7 Patterns Multiplier without giving up one of your normal Rounds.

antiSynergies.why: Only 1 spin per Round, so each sacrifice gives just +1 Patterns Multiplier.
One button fires both: pressing for Midas Touch also ends the Round, and a sacrifice wastes a charged Midas Touch; keep one of them in a drawer.

assumptions: Assumed the Patterns Multiplier change is permanent, like the Cross it is made from; the wiki notes it is the only source of a negative multiplier.
Value is modelled as one sacrificed Round per Deadline (-1 Round of income, +7 Patterns Multiplier); players with spare Rounds can sacrifice more.
Assumed a press fires every charged Red Button charm at once, as the button normally does.
Wiki: the Corpse piece only drops from a 666 and is discarded if it is still in a drawer when the Deadline ends, so the fusion must happen in that Deadline.

summary: Surgery (Corpse Right Arm + Ankh): Charms discarded during a Round, such as ones that break, come back in the next store restocks to buy again.
tip: Makes one-shot Charms repeatable: buy back Holy Bible, One Trick Pony or the Peppers after they break. They return as normal store offers, so you pay again; Weird Clock is excluded.

effects.text: Charms discarded during a Round (for example ones that break) appear again in the next store restock(s). Weird Clock is excluded, and only Charms that can appear in the store come back.

synergies.why: When it breaks after blocking a 666, it is back in the next restock for 1 ticket.
Buy it back after it breaks for another guaranteed Jackpot.
Comes back after its 9 activations, ready for 9 more Luck +7 spins.
Every break adds a Beetle stack, and the broken Charm can be bought and broken again.
With Sacrifice, Sin and Eternal Rest it fuses into Apocalypse, which restarts the run keeping your table.

assumptions: Assumed 'discarded during a Round' covers Charms that break or discard themselves mid-Round (Holy Bible, Peppers, One Trick Pony), and that they come back at their normal price.
Unclear whether Charms that decay away at a Round's end (Fruit Basket, Personal Trainer) or Charms you sell yourself count.

summary: Surgery (Corpse Right Leg + Evil Deal): your coins and tickets double at the end of every Round, but both are set to 0 when the Deadline ends.
tip: Hold coins so they double each Round, then pay the debt (deposits stop at the debt) and spend tickets before the Deadline ends. From Deadline 7 a 666 takes all coins in hand: bring protection.

effects.note: Coins in hand double at the end of every Round.
Tickets double at the end of every Round.
Coins still in hand when the Deadline ends are lost.
Tickets still held when the Deadline ends are lost.

synergies.why: You cannot deposit before the last Round anyway, so the doubling applies to everything you earn.
Blocks the 666 that would take your whole held pile from Deadline 7.
Tickets double every Round, so its +1 Patterns Multiplier per 15 tickets climbs during the Deadline; spend them before it ends.
Tickets double every Round, so its multiplier climbs during the Deadline; spend them before it ends.
A sacrificed Round still ends, so your held coins double without playing a spin.
With Sacrifice, Resurrection and Eternal Rest it fuses into Apocalypse, which restarts the run keeping your table.

antiSynergies.why: Its forced 666s take all the coins you are holding from Deadline 7.
It pays on tickets held when the Deadline ends, but Sin wipes them.
Interest is paid on deposited coins, but Sin wants them held until the end, so Interest and each Cat payout stay small.

assumptions: Doubles coins in hand, not coins deposited; deposits are capped at the debt (wiki), so surplus coins are lost when the Deadline ends instead of carrying over.
Unknown whether the Deadline Bonus and end-of-Deadline tickets arrive before or after the reset.
Interest is a share of the deposit, so holding coins to double them gives up most Interest income.

Engine: with your coins in hand unknown it assumes a small purse (a quarter of a Round's income), so the doubling shows only about +15%; held as Sin intends, early-Round coins grow x4-x8 (about x2.3-x4.7 more coins toward the debt per Deadline). Entering your coins in hand lets it see this. Tickets get no value.

summary: Surgery (Corpse Left Leg + Weird Clock): every Charm that is not an ingredient of some Surgery recipe is banned from the store.
tip: Shrinks the store to about 50 recipe ingredients, so parts for your next fusion show up far more often. It also bans strong non-recipe Charms: keep it in a drawer when not hunting parts.

effects.text: Only Charms listed in a Surgery recipe can appear in the store (54 of the 145 store Charms, minus banned ingredients such as Weird Clock).

synergies.why: Parts for more fusions show up, and Eternal Rest counts as a Surgery charm itself (+10%).
With Sacrifice, Resurrection and Sin it fuses into Apocalypse, and it makes those parts' other ingredients (Cross, Ankh, Evil Deal) show up more often.

assumptions: Assumed 'Any Charm' recipes (Garbage, Trash Can, Dumpster) do not count as listing every Charm.
Assumed it only works while on the table, like other charms, so a drawer switches it off.

summary: Surgery (Sacrifice + Resurrection + Sin + Eternal Rest): you die at once, then start a new run with the same memory card and all your table Charms.
tip: Not a power pick: it ends the current run (a secret ending, counted as a death). Make it to carry a full late-game table into a fresh run; extra slots from the phone call do not carry over.

effects.text: When created, the run ends immediately (counted as a death, with a secret ending). The next run starts with the same memory card and every charm that was on the table except Apocalypse; everything else resets.

synergies.why: One of its four ingredients, all fused from a Corpse piece.
One of its four ingredients, all fused from a Corpse piece.
One of its four ingredients, all fused from a Corpse piece.
One of its four ingredients, all fused from a Corpse piece.

antiSynergies.why: Its extra slots are not carried over, so the most recently placed charms beyond them are removed in the next run.

assumptions: Wiki notes: charms beyond the normal space from 'Please don't throw my stuff away!' are removed in the next run, most recently placed first.
Its value lies in the next run, which the Build Helper does not model, so it is rated as a run-ender.
